topics.name: Number System
topics.description: Types of numbers, place value, integers, rationals and the properties that everything else in arithmetic is built on.
topics.whyItMatters: Number system is the vocabulary of the whole subject. Remainders, factors and properties recur in every other topic.

topics.name: Divisibility
topics.description: Divisibility rules, remainders and quick tests that save calculation time.

topics.name: Factors and Multiples
topics.description: Prime factorisation, counting factors, and how multiples behave.

topics.name: HCF and LCM
topics.description: Highest common factor, lowest common multiple, and the problems that hide them.

topics.name: Remainders and Cyclicity
topics.description: Remainders of sums, products and huge powers, unit digits and last two digits, the theorems of Fermat, Euler and Wilson, and numbers found from their remainders.
topics.whyItMatters: A CAT, XAT and placement favourite, and a regular in SSC: "the remainder when 7¹⁰⁰ is divided by 5" or "the unit digit of 13²⁰²⁶" takes seconds once you know the cycle, and minutes if you do not.

topics.name: Factorials
topics.description: Trailing zeros, the highest power of a prime or composite in n!, the size of n!, which numbers divide it, and sums of factorials.
topics.whyItMatters: Trailing zeros and prime powers in n! appear in CAT, SNAP and placement tests almost every year, and the counting is quick once you see the layers.

topics.name: Simplification
topics.description: BODMAS, fraction handling and structured ways to reduce messy expressions.

topics.name: Speed Maths
topics.description: Multiplying by 5, 25, 125, 111 and 99, the base method, cross multiplication, percentage–fraction swaps, digit-sum checks and quick division.
topics.whyItMatters: Bank and SSC prelims give about 20 seconds a calculation. These methods turn long multiplication into one line, and the nines check catches slips before they cost marks.

topics.name: Squares, Cubes and Roots
topics.description: Squares near a base, splitting, cubes of two-digit numbers, square and cube roots of perfect powers, roots of decimals, estimates and perfect-square tests.
topics.whyItMatters: Square roots of four- and five-digit numbers and cubes of two-digit numbers turn up throughout simplification and approximation sets in bank, SSC and railway exams.

topics.name: Approximation
topics.description: Estimating answers fast enough to beat the clock without losing accuracy.

topics.name: Fractions
topics.description: Comparing, converting and operating on fractions with confidence.

topics.name: Decimals
topics.description: Decimal arithmetic, recurring decimals and conversions.

topics.name: Surds and Indices
topics.description: Laws of exponents, roots, and simplifying surd expressions.

topics.name: Percentages
topics.description: The single most reused idea in aptitude: parts of a whole, increases, decreases and reverse calculations.
topics.whyItMatters: Percentages sit underneath profit and loss, interest, data interpretation and most comparison questions. Every hour here pays off in five other topics.

topics.name: Ratio and Proportion
topics.description: Comparing quantities, splitting amounts and working with proportional relationships.
topics.whyItMatters: Ratios are how exam setters hide numbers. Once you can read a ratio as a set of parts, mixtures, partnerships and work problems become routine.

topics.name: Direct and Inverse Proportion
topics.description: Recognising when quantities rise together and when one falls as the other rises.

topics.name: Averages
topics.description: Arithmetic mean, how averages shift, and the classic replacement problems.
topics.whyItMatters: Averages appear directly in questions and indirectly whenever a total has to be redistributed. The replacement pattern alone shows up every year.

topics.name: Weighted Average
topics.description: Combining groups of different sizes into one representative value.

topics.name: Mixtures and Alligation
topics.description: Blending quantities at different rates, and the alligation shortcut.
topics.whyItMatters: Alligation turns a two-equation problem into a one-line ratio. It is the highest speed-gain shortcut in arithmetic.

topics.name: Profit, Loss and Discount
topics.description: Cost price, selling price, markup and discount chains as they appear in real trade problems.
topics.whyItMatters: Trade problems are the most common application of percentages, and successive discount chains are a favourite trap.

topics.name: Simple Interest
topics.description: Interest on the original principal only — the entry point to all lending problems.
topics.whyItMatters: Simple interest is the cleanest way to practise substituting into a formula with unit conversion — and it is the base case for compound interest.

topics.name: Compound Interest
topics.description: Interest on interest, compounding frequency, and growth-rate problems.
topics.whyItMatters: Compounding is the difference between a small rate and a large outcome, and it powers population, depreciation and growth questions too.

topics.name: Partnership
topics.description: Splitting profit by capital and time invested.

topics.name: Time and Work
topics.description: Work rates, combined effort, and efficiency comparisons.
topics.whyItMatters: Work-rate thinking transfers straight to pipes, wages and speed. Learning to work in units of work per day removes most of the difficulty.

topics.name: Pipes and Cisterns
topics.description: Filling and emptying rates — time and work in a tank.

topics.name: Time, Speed and Distance
topics.description: The relationship behind every motion problem, plus average speed and relative speed.
topics.whyItMatters: Motion problems reward a single relationship used carefully. Average speed and relative speed are where most marks are lost.

topics.name: Trains
topics.description: Relative speed with length: crossing poles, platforms and other trains.

topics.name: Boats and Streams
topics.description: Upstream and downstream speeds and the still-water relationship.

topics.name: Races
topics.description: Head starts, beats-by distances and dead heats.

topics.name: Problems on Ages
topics.description: Turning "years ago" and "years hence" statements into equations.
topics.whyItMatters: Age questions are equation-forming practice in disguise: translate the sentence correctly and the algebra is easy.

topics.name: Work and Wages
topics.description: Paying people in proportion to the work they actually do.

topics.name: Calendars
topics.description: Odd days, leap years and finding the day of the week.

topics.name: Clocks
topics.description: Angles between hands, coincidences and gaining/losing clocks.

topics.name: Unit Conversions
topics.description: Moving between units without losing a factor of ten.

topics.name: Algebraic Expressions
topics.description: Terms, coefficients and manipulating expressions safely.

topics.name: Linear Equations
topics.description: Forming and solving one-variable equations from word problems.

topics.name: Simultaneous Linear Equations
topics.description: Two unknowns, two equations, and the fastest route to both.

topics.name: Quadratic Equations
topics.description: Factorisation, the formula, and the meaning of the discriminant.

topics.name: Quadratic Comparison (x vs y)
topics.description: The bank-paper favourite: solve two equations and decide how x and y compare, from five fixed answers.
topics.whyItMatters: IBPS and SBI prelims set about five of these in every paper; with the routine they take under a minute each.

topics.name: Algebraic Identities
topics.description: The standard identities that turn long expansions into one line.

topics.name: Inequalities
topics.description: Solving and reasoning with inequality statements.

topics.name: Sequences
topics.description: Spotting the rule behind a list of numbers: differences, ratios, special and interleaved patterns, and wrong terms.

topics.name: Arithmetic Progression
topics.description: Common difference, nth term and sum of a series with constant steps.
topics.whyItMatters: APs formalise "constant change", which is exactly what instalments, salaries and seating problems describe.

topics.name: Geometric Progression
topics.description: Common ratio, nth term and sums including infinite series.

topics.name: Logarithms
topics.description: Log laws and using them to unwind exponents.

topics.name: Functions and Basic Graphs
topics.description: Reading, evaluating and sketching simple functions.

topics.name: Lines and Angles
topics.description: Angle relationships formed by intersecting and parallel lines.

topics.name: Triangles
topics.description: Properties, congruence, similarity and the Pythagorean relationship.

topics.name: Quadrilaterals
topics.description: Squares, rectangles, parallelograms, trapezia and their properties.

topics.name: Polygons
topics.description: Interior and exterior angles, diagonals and regular polygons.

topics.name: Circles
topics.description: Chords, tangents, arcs, sectors and circle theorems.

topics.name: Coordinate Geometry
topics.description: Distance, midpoint, slope and the equation of a line.

topics.name: Perimeter and Area
topics.description: Boundary length and area for the standard plane figures.

topics.name: 2D Mensuration
topics.description: Composite plane figures and shaded-region problems.

topics.name: 3D Mensuration
topics.description: Cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones and spheres.

topics.name: Volume and Surface Area
topics.description: Capacity and surface problems, including melting and recasting.

topics.name: Trigonometry
topics.description: Sine, cosine and tangent, the standard angles, complementary angles and the Pythagorean identities.
topics.whyItMatters: SSC, CDS, NDA and AFCAT papers ask several trigonometry questions, and most reduce to the standard-angle table and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

topics.name: Heights and Distances
topics.description: Angles of elevation and depression, towers, shadows and ladders: trigonometry on real objects.
topics.whyItMatters: A favourite of SSC and defence papers: one right triangle and tan 30°, 45° or 60° settle almost every question.

topics.name: Fundamental Principle of Counting
topics.description: Multiplying and adding choices — the base of all counting.

topics.name: Permutations
topics.description: Arrangements where order matters, including restrictions and repetition.
topics.whyItMatters: Counting arrangements correctly is a skill of classification: decide whether order matters before you touch a formula.

topics.name: Combinations
topics.description: Selections where order does not matter.
topics.whyItMatters: Selection problems appear in probability, geometry and data questions. Getting nCr right unlocks all three.

topics.name: Probability
topics.description: Favourable over total, independent and mutually exclusive events.
topics.whyItMatters: Probability is where careful counting meets careful reading. Most errors are counting errors, not probability errors.

topics.name: Set Theory
topics.description: Unions, intersections, complements and cardinality.

topics.name: Venn Diagrams
topics.description: Two- and three-set problems solved visually.

topics.name: Tables
topics.description: Reading tabular data accurately and answering multi-step questions from it.
topics.whyItMatters: Data interpretation is mostly percentage and ratio work under time pressure. Accurate reading beats fast calculation.

topics.name: Bar Graphs
topics.description: Comparing categories and reading values off bars.

topics.name: Line Graphs
topics.description: Trends, growth and change over time.

topics.name: Pie Charts
topics.description: Turning angles and shares into quantities.

topics.name: Caselet DI
topics.description: Extracting structured data from a paragraph of text.

topics.name: Mixed and Radar Charts
topics.description: Radar charts, bar-and-line combinations, tables with missing values, and multi-step questions across charts.
topics.whyItMatters: Bank PO mains papers build their hardest data sets from these chart types; the reading rules are simple once seen.

topics.name: Data Sufficiency
topics.description: Deciding whether the given statements are enough to answer.

topics.name: Mean, Median and Mode
topics.description: Three centres of a dataset and when each one matters.

topics.name: Grouped Data and Graphs
topics.description: Frequency tables and class marks, histograms, frequency polygons and ogives, and the mean, median and mode of grouped data (direct, assumed-mean and step-deviation methods).
topics.whyItMatters: CDS, NDA and SSC CGL Tier 2 set grouped frequency tables every year: the mean by step deviation, the median and mode classes, a missing frequency, or a value read off an ogive.

topics.name: Weighted Mean
topics.description: Averaging when the pieces carry different weight.

topics.name: Measures of Dispersion
topics.description: Range, deviation and spread at aptitude level.

topics.name: Seating Arrangement
topics.description: People in a row, in two facing rows or around a table: turn clues into one arrangement and read off neighbours, opposites and positions.
topics.whyItMatters: Seating sets are a fixture of bank prelims and mains reasoning, and they train the habit every puzzle needs: fix the certain clue first, then branch on the cases.

topics.name: Puzzles
topics.description: Floors, stacked boxes, days of the week and person–city–colour grids, solved by placing what is certain and eliminating the rest.
topics.whyItMatters: Puzzles carry the most marks in bank reasoning sections and appear in CAT and placement DILR. A tidy grid and the case method turn a long set into quick marks.

topics.name: Syllogism
topics.description: All, some and no statements; which conclusions definitely follow, either-or pairs, and possibilities, decided with Venn diagrams.
topics.whyItMatters: Syllogisms come in almost every bank, SSC and railway paper. With the least-overlap diagram they take under a minute each.

topics.name: Inequalities (Reasoning)
topics.description: Chains like P ≥ Q > R = S and coded symbols: which conclusions are definitely true, either-or cases, and the missing sign.
topics.whyItMatters: Bank prelims set four or five of these in a row. Once the path rule is automatic they are among the fastest marks in the paper.

topics.name: Blood Relations
topics.description: Family statements, family-tree puzzles and coded relations: name how two people are related, count generations, and spot what cannot be known.
topics.whyItMatters: Asked in bank, SSC, railway and placement tests, often inside a puzzle. Drawing the tree first prevents almost every mistake.
